subject: history_social
passage: In August 1858, after several failed attempts, workers finished laying a telegraph cable across the floor of the Atlantic Ocean, linking Ireland and Newfoundland. Celebrations broke out in cities on both sides of the ocean, and Queen Victoria sent a message of congratulations to US President James Buchanan. Yet the cable was disappointing in practice: her short message took more than sixteen hours to transmit, and within about three weeks the cable had stopped working entirely. A lasting connection across the Atlantic was not achieved until 1866.
stem: According to the text, what was true of the telegraph cable completed in 1858?

choices.A: It was the first of several cables that worked reliably across the Atlantic.
choices.B: It was celebrated mainly in Britain, which had paid for its construction.
choices.C: It carried messages across the Atlantic in minutes for a short time.
choices.D: It was widely celebrated, though it carried messages slowly and soon failed.

explanation.why: The text says "celebrations broke out in cities on both sides of the ocean," but then turns with "Yet": a short message took "more than sixteen hours," and the cable stopped working within about three weeks. The correct choice combines the celebration with these two problems.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The 1858 cable failed within weeks, and a lasting link came only in 1866.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Celebrations happened "on both sides of the ocean," and the text never says who paid for the cable.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says a short message took more than sixteen hours, not minutes.
explanation.D: Correct. The cable was celebrated widely, but it was very slow and stopped working within about three weeks.
